value: Study cohort: 41 healthy controls, 56 pre-hypertensive, 99 hypertensive Chinese individuals from Kailuan Group
Blood pressure classifications: control ≤125/80 mmHg, pHTN 125-139/80-89 mmHg, HTN ≥140/≥90 mmHg
Metagenomic sequencing generated 1211 Gb total with average 6.18 ± 1.43 million reads per sample
Metabolomic analysis on 124 subjects: 30 controls, 31 pHTN, 63 HTN
Fecal microbiota transplantation to germ-free mice (n=5 control, n=10 HTN recipients)
Blood pressure measurement in recipient mice by tail-cuff method at 10 weeks post-transplantation
HTN mice exhibited significantly higher SBP (P=0.018), DBP (P=0.019), MBP (P=0.014)
Exclusion criteria: cancer, heart failure, renal failure, smoking, stroke, peripheral artery disease, antibiotics/probiotics within 8 weeks
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: Cohort of 41 healthy controls, 56 subjects with pHTN, 99 individuals with primary HTN. Total of 1211 Gb 125-bp paired-end reads. HTN mice exhibited significantly higher SBP, DBP, and MBP.

extraction_warnings: Paper does not report individual-level participant demographics (age, sex, ancestry) for most samples; only aggregate group-level statistics available
Sample identifiers are not provided in the paper; generated synthetic IDs based on group membership (HC=healthy control, PHT=pre-hypertension, HTN=hypertension) with sequential numbering
No NCBI accession numbers reported for the metagenomic sequencing data in the provided text
Paper reports cohort-level statistics (n=41 controls, n=56 pHTN, n=99 HTN) but does not provide individual sample metadata; sample_level granularity reflects this limitation
Validation cohort (n=6 samples from type 2 diabetes study) was not included in sample list as it uses external data
Batch 1 returned granularity='subgroup_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 1 subgroups ['Healthy controls', 'Pre-hypertension (pHTN)', 'Primary hypertension (HTN)'] differ from batch 0 []; kept batch 0.
Age information is not reported for any participant groups, limiting demographic characterization.
Gender distribution is mentioned as discrepant but specific values and analysis by gender are not provided.
BMI values are mentioned in correlation analyses but not reported as group means/medians.
FMT donors were limited (n=3: 2 HTN, 1 control), constraining generalizability of transplantation findings.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

The schema requested ECOG performance status, overall survival, and tumor measurements, which are not applicable to this hypertension microbiota study. These fields are cancer-specific and were correctly marked 'not_reported'.
Biomarker values are primarily directional (elevated/decreased) with statistical p-values rather than absolute quantitative measurements, reflecting the metagenomic/metabolomic analysis approach.

The study reports subgroup-level data (controls vs pHTN vs HTN) but the extraction granularity is study_level because the schema does not support nested subgroup structures for most fields. Blood pressure classification thresholds and comparative statistics are documented in 'uncurated_metadata'.
Multiple bacterial taxa and metabolite biomarkers were identified; the extraction captures the most salient and repeatedly mentioned ones identified across the paper.
